around.headline: Bengaluru woman alleges Rs 2.5 crore fraud by self-styled godman
around.summary: A woman has filed a police case alleging a self-styled godman defrauded her of ₹2.5 crore. Be cautious of anyone offering spiritual 'fixes' for money or family troubles that require cash payments — verify credentials before parting with any sum.

around.headline: Driver robbed at knifepoint in broad daylight at busy Bengaluru junction
around.summary: A driver was robbed at knifepoint in daylight at a busy city junction. Stay alert at signals and junctions, especially if carrying cash, and flag suspicious loitering to nearby police or traffic police booths.

around.headline: Elderly pedestrians killed in separate bus accidents this week
around.summary: An 86-year-old was run over by a KSRTC bus and another elderly man was knocked down by a city bus while crossing roads in Bengaluru. Use marked crossings or skywalks where available, and make eye contact with drivers before crossing near buses.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: Landslip disrupts Mangaluru–Bengaluru rail traffic
around.summary: A landslip on the ghat section has forced cancellations and diversions on the Mangaluru–Bengaluru rail route. If you have a train booked on this route, check its current status before heading to the station.
around.source: The New Indian Express, The Times of India

around.headline: Lokayukta sets August 15 deadline to clear Bengaluru's garbage black spots
around.summary: The Lokayukta has given BBMP until August 15 to clear remaining garbage black spots, while CM Shivakumar has separately warned property owners to clean up waste on vacant plots or face government action. Owners of empty plots should expect scrutiny over the next two weeks.

around.summary: New trading timings for Indian stock markets take effect from today. If you trade regularly, double-check NSE/BSE session hours before placing orders.

street_smart.title: A relative introduces you to a well-known 'godman' who says he can end your family's bad luck and money troubles — but only if you follow his instructions exactly and keep it between the two of you. He asks for ₹50,000 in cash today for a special ritual. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's news — a Bengaluru woman alleges she was defrauded of ₹2.5 crore by a self-styled godman, and a case has been registered (The Indian Express).
street_smart.situation: He's calm, well-spoken, and clearly trusted by your relative, who's vouching hard for him. He says doubting him now, or discussing this with anyone outside the room, will 'break the ritual's effect.' You have the cash on you. What do you do?

choices.text: Firmly decline to pay, suggest addressing the actual problem through real channels (a financial advisor, family budgeting, or debt counselling), and note his name/address in case you need to report him later.
choices.feedback: Correct. Any 'spiritual fix' that demands cash and secrecy from your own family is a red flag, not a ritual requirement. If you already suspect fraud — even without paying — you can note details and report to your local police station or the Karnataka cyber crime helpline; that's exactly how the ₹2.5 crore Bengaluru case got registered.

choices.text: Pay the ₹50,000 now since he came recommended by a trusted relative, and refusing might offend the family or 'undo' the ritual.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A trusted relative's recommendation is exactly how these schemes spread — each payment is followed by a request for a bigger one because 'the ritual needs more to work,' and the secrecy rule stops you from checking in with anyone before it's too late. This mirrors how the Bengaluru woman was allegedly defrauded of ₹2.5 crore.

choices.text: Offer a smaller 'trial' amount first, just to see if anything actually changes before committing more.
choices.feedback: Risky. Even a small first payment builds trust and a sense of investment that makes it psychologically harder to walk away later — graduated asks are a deliberate tactic, not a compromise that protects you.

choices.text: Confront him loudly on the spot and order him to leave immediately.
choices.feedback: Risky. A public confrontation can escalate into conflict or threats without giving you any real evidence trail. A calm refusal, followed by a proper report if needed, protects you better than a scene.

takeaways: Any request for cash tied to secrecy from your own family is a red flag — genuine advice never needs to be hidden from people close to you.
Verify credentials before engaging anyone offering spiritual or ritual 'fixes' for money problems, and never make large cash payments without a receipt or paper trail.
To report a suspected fraud, contact your local police station or call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 / file at cybercrime.gov.in — police do register and act on these cases.

quiz.question: Per today's news, by when has the Lokayukta directed BBMP to clear Bengaluru's remaining garbage black spots?
quiz.why: The Lokayukta is Karnataka's anti-corruption ombudsman and can direct civic bodies like BBMP on compliance matters such as sanitation lapses.

quiz.question: How much money did a Bengaluru woman allege she lost to a self-styled godman, per today's news?
quiz.why: Karnataka has a dedicated law — the Karnataka Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and other Inhuman, Evil and Aghori Practices and Black Magic Act, 2017 — aimed at cases involving exploitation through superstition.

quiz.question: Which reservoir is helping ease Karnataka's water stress amid the ongoing Cauvery dispute, per today's news?
quiz.why: Kabini, on a Cauvery tributary in Mysuru district, is one of four major reservoirs — along with KRS, Harangi and Hemavati — that feed the Cauvery river system.

quiz.question: Which regulatory body oversees India's stock exchanges, such as the NSE and BSE?
quiz.why: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India), set up in 1992, regulates market intermediaries and protects investor interests alongside overseeing exchange operations.

quiz.question: Roughly how high above sea level does Bengaluru sit?
quiz.why: Bengaluru's elevation of roughly 900m on the Deccan plateau is a big reason the city has a milder climate than much of peninsular India despite its low latitude.
